$meta.description: Normative machine-readable registry of the Stencil LLM op-plan surface (llm-contract.md §1-§13). Every surface's validator is TABLE-DRIVEN from this file: profile membership, key schemas (types, enums, ranges, caps, token grammars) and the cross-field rules (forms/together/minFields/onlyWith/requiredWith) are read from here; surfaces keep only their normalizers, executors and the few native rules named in "rules". Recorded divergences are surface-specific by design (surfaceKeys, surfaces, forbidden.perSurface) — see opRegistry.README.md for the schema.
$meta.guard: browser/tests/opRegistryCanon.test.js pins this file to the live browser structures and the fixture corpus; every surface's fixture walker asserts its table-driven validator against the corpus

extension.note: extension-profile extras from browser-extension/src/llm/opPlan.js LIMITS; the extension has no frameIndices limit (it registers no frame op at top level)

describe.CROP_TOKEN: a crop token (number with optional % / px / cm / in, leading "-" from the far side)
describe.PAGE_FORMAT: a lowercase ISO name a0–a10, b0–b10 or c0–c10

regexes.note: Flag-free sources so non-regex surfaces (cli, mcp) can hand-match them: case-insensitivity is spelled out in the pattern. CROP_ASPECT encodes the > 0 rule; the formula charsets apply to non-empty expressions only ("blankOk"). "describe" is the wording validators use in their error messages.

notes.openFile: desktop-only (entry surfaces: desktop, cli) — the browser skips it as unknown (fixture 052)
notes.voiceChat: browser-only (entry surfaces: browser) — the desktop skips it as unknown (fixtures 218/219)

notes.accent: cli-only (entry surfaces) — pystencil skips it as unknown (fixtures 165/167 + the generated accent cases)
notes.reconnect: cli-only (entry surfaces) — pystencil skips it as unknown (fixture 055)
notes.copy: cli-only (entry surfaces); the console copy takes no fields (surfaceKeys.cli)
notes.reset: cli parses reset but never advertises it (no bullet); pystencil advertises it in the console block

notes.filter: the extension's filter is the panel-list filter (entry filter.extension), NOT the §2 image filter

forbidden.note: The canonical §13 categories as the browser names them; every surface implements the same categories with its own name list below. Enforcement differs: cli and mcp HARD-FAIL a plan naming a forbidden op, every other surface skips the unknown name at parse and rejects it at the executor (fixtures 207-217 knownDivergence). Notable membership drift: "endpoint" is list-forbidden only on cli (fixture 214); "chat"/"shareTabs" hard-fail only on mcp (215, 216); mcp also forbids clearChat/chatPersist (it registers no chat surface); bot forbids delete/removeProject/clearProjects/expire — names other profiles register as ops.

divergence: preview RENDERING differs (editors render option actions, the extension only shows scanIndex pictures, consoles/bot show none) — validation is identical

actions.note: preview actions — ordinary §2 actions validated as "inside variants or previews"; a misplaced op costs the option its picture, not the plan

schema.note: Uniform on every surface since the table-driving pass (fixtures 103/104 lost their knownDivergence). Surfaces that render no previews still VALIDATE option images/actions, then drop the picture with a warning.

ops.name: crop
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"crop","spec":{"x1":"10%","x2":"-10%","aspect":"3:4"}} — move edges inward;
  tokens are numbers with optional unit % / px / cm / in; a leading "-" measures from the
  opposite side. Include only the edges you want to move. For a target aspect ratio add
  "aspect":"W:H" INSIDE "spec", never beside it (portrait "3:4", album/landscape "4:3",
  square "1:1") — the editor cuts the resolved crop to that exact ratio about its centre,
  so NEVER derive ratio tokens yourself; combine it with edge tokens when a specific
  region should be kept.

spec.note: needs at least one of x1/x2/y1/y2/aspect; unknown spec keys fail the plan

aspect.note: §3.2 tolerance (native rule cropAspectFold): "aspect" beside "spec" is folded into it when the spec lacks one; a conflicting duplicate fails the plan

divergence: console (cli + pystencil): the spec also accepts "album": true — derive the missing crop axis from the page format in landscape orientation (surfaceKeys.cli / surfaceKeys.pystencil); no other surface takes it
extension: crop exists only inside open.actions, with spec keys x1/x2/y1/y2 only — no "aspect" (inside or beside the spec) and no action-level fold
console (cli + pystencil): "album" alone (no edge/aspect key) is rejected natively — album is a modifier, not an edge, though spec.minFields counts it

console.addendum:
- The crop op's "spec" also takes "album": true — derive the missing crop axis from
  the page format in landscape orientation (the console's '/crop … album').

album.note: console-only: derive the missing crop axis from the page format in landscape orientation

aspect.note: §3.2 tolerance (native rule cropAspectFold): "aspect" beside "spec" is folded into it when the spec lacks one; a conflicting duplicate fails the plan

album.note: console-only: derive the missing crop axis from the page format in landscape orientation

aspect.note: §3.2 tolerance (native rule cropAspectFold): "aspect" beside "spec" is folded into it when the spec lacks one; a conflicting duplicate fails the plan

ops.name: rotate
ops.bullet: - {"op":"rotate","dir":"left"|"right","times":1..3} — quarter turns only.

ops.name: filter
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"filter","mode":"none"|"bw"|"sepia"|"invert"|"contour"|"custom","tint":"#rrggbb"}
  — "custom" is a duotone tint and requires "tint"; "contour" is edge detection.

tint.note: required with mode "custom", forbidden with every other mode

divergence: extension: the name "filter" is a DIFFERENT op there (the panel-list filter — see the filter.extension entry); this §2 image-filter shape is invalid at the extension top level (fixture 069) and allowed only inside open.actions

ops.name: layout
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"layout","lines":[{"points":[{"x":0,"y":0},...],"color":"#FFFF00","thickness":2,
  "pointSize":4,"style":"solid"|"dashed"|"dotted","locked":false,"fillColor":"transparent"}]}
  — draw annotation polylines in image-pixel coordinates. When asked to extract lines,
  shapes, or structure from an attached image, answer with this op. An empty "lines"
  array REMOVES every drawn line — that is what "clear/remove the lines" means.

lines.note: an empty array removes every drawn line

bulletVariants.mcp:
- {"op":"layout","lines":[{"points":[{"x":0,"y":0},...],"color":"#FFFF00","thickness":2,
  "pointSize":4,"style":"solid"|"dashed"|"dotted","locked":false,"fillColor":"transparent"}]}
  — draw annotation polylines in image-pixel coordinates. When asked to extract lines,
  shapes, or structure from an attached image, answer with this op.

divergence: desktop: a line with an empty points array fails at parse (native post-check); the browser baseline keeps the empty line

ops.name: formula
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"formula","axis":"x"|"y","expr":"x*2+10"} — coordinate transform; single variable
  matching the axis; operators + - * / ** and parentheses only. An empty "expr" clears
  that axis; {"op":"formula","enabled":false} switches formulas OFF entirely.

enabled.note: rides ALONE — mutually exclusive with axis+expr; false switches formulas off

ops.note: exactly one form: axis+expr, or enabled alone
divergence: mcp: "enabled" alone and the empty-expr clear are ACCEPTED but execute as inert no-ops with a note (a one-shot headless run has no persistent formula state); fixtures 011/012 agree on all surfaces

ops.name: page
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"page","format":"a4"} — ISO page formats a0–a10, b0–b10, c0–c10 — or a custom
  size: {"op":"page","width":20,"height":30} in centimetres (one form or the other).
ops.note: exactly one form: "format", or "width"+"height" in centimetres

ops.name: blank
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"blank","color":"#ffffff","format":"a4"} — create a blank page; explicit
  centimetre dims ride as "width"/"height" instead of "format".

width.note: rides together with height; overrides format

height.note: rides together with width; overrides format

divergence: desktop: additionally rejects a color NAME that is not a real CSS colour (core::parseColor), where every other surface accepts any alphabetic word (fixture 137 knownDivergence) — a native post-check, not a schema difference

ops.name: undo
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"undo","steps":1} / {"op":"redo","steps":1} — step this surface's edit history.
  "Undo that" means {"op":"undo"}; steps count history entries, which can be finer
  than one request.
ops.note: not registered on mcp — a one-shot headless tool has no edit history to step

ops.name: redo
ops.note: not registered on mcp — a one-shot headless tool has no edit history to step

ops.name: frame
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"frame","index":0} or {"op":"frame","indices":[0,30,60]} — pick video frame(s);
  only valid when the current input is a video.
ops.note: exactly one of index / indices; only valid when the current input is a video

ops.name: image
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"image","index":1} — switch the working image to the Nth image attached to THIS
  message (1-based, in attachment order); coordinates in later actions are in THAT
  image's pixel frame. Only valid when the user attached images. Use it to edit several
  attached images in one plan, giving each image its OWN actions.

ops.name: save
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"save","name":"portrait 1"} — save the current image with its drawn lines as a
  project. When the user asks to process several images and keep the results, finish
  each image's actions with a "save" before switching to the next: image 1, its edits,
  save, image 2, its edits, save, …

path.note: a local destination (folder or file name; ".stencil" saves the whole project, an image extension saves the picture); trimmed, a URL scheme is rejected, "" is dropped

divergence: "path" acceptance is uniform since the Phase-6 reconciliation: every surface carrying save validates it (string ≤ MAX_PATH_CHARS, trimmed, no URL scheme, "" ≡ absent) — fixture 024 covers all four profiles

"path" execution honor split: desktop and cli honor the destination (under the user-echo guard — only a path the user themselves wrote); mcp honors it relative to the run's output_dir (traversal-guarded: absolute, ".." or "~" paths note-and-fall-back; ".stencil" is a file, anything else a folder); browser, pystencil and bot accept the field but note-and-skip at execution, saving to the usual place

bulletVariants.desktop:
- {"op":"save","name":"portrait 1","path":"~/Downloads"} — save the current image with its
  drawn lines. "path" is optional and may be a folder or a file name (".stencil" saves the
  whole project, an image extension saves the picture); with no path it becomes a project in
  the editor. ONLY a path the user themselves wrote in this conversation — never invent,
  complete or rewrite one. When the user asks to process several images and keep the results,
  finish each image's actions with a "save" before switching to the next: image 1, its edits,
  save, image 2, its edits, save, …
bulletVariants.cli:
- {"op":"save","name":"portrait 1","path":"~/Downloads"} — save the current image with its
  drawn lines. `path` is optional and may be a folder or a file name (".stencil" saves the
  whole project, an image extension saves the picture); with no path it writes a project
  into the working directory. ONLY a path the user themselves wrote in this conversation —
  never invent, complete or rewrite one. When the user asks to process several images and
  keep the results, finish each image's actions with a "save" before switching to the
  next: image 1, its edits, save, image 2, its edits, save, …

ops.name: theme
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"theme","mode":"light"|"dark"} — switch the editor between light and dark
  ONLY; "mode" takes no other value. A COLOUR ("make the theme cyan") is the accent
  op below, never this one.
divergence: extension: a different enum — "mode" also accepts "system" (follows the OS setting); "system" is invalid in the editor (fixtures 066, 070)

bulletVariants.extension:
- {"op":"theme","mode":"dark"|"light"|"system"} — switch the Stencil panel's own theme
  ("system" follows the OS setting). This changes the panel's appearance only.

ops.name: accent
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"accent","color":"#7c3aed"} — set the editor accent colour. "color" must be
  a #rrggbb hex, so translate colour names yourself (cyan = "#00ffff").
ops.also:
- "accent" also accepts {"op":"accent","preset":"green"} — a named preset persists and
  syncs; use a preset when the user names a colour that has one.

preset.note: non-empty; browser trims + lowercases; an unknown preset NAME is a note + skip at run

divergence: console membership is cli-only: pystencil does not register accent, so its form errors fall to the unknown-op skip there (fixtures 165-167 knownDivergence)
extension: keeps the preset case as typed (no lowercasing) and resolves a hex to the nearest of the panel's preset accents

bulletVariants.console:
- {"op":"accent","color":"#7c3aed"} — set the console's colour theme (its accent).
  "color" must be a #rrggbb hex, so translate colour names yourself (cyan =
  "#00ffff"). The console has no light/dark mode — a theme request means this op.
- "accent" also accepts {"op":"accent","preset":"green"} — one of the console's
  named /theme presets; use a preset when the user names a colour that has one.
bulletVariants.extension:
- {"op":"accent","color":"#7c3aed"} — set the Stencil panel's own accent colour. "color"
  must be # + 6 hex digits (the nearest of the panel's preset accents applies); also
  accepts {"op":"accent","preset":"green"} — a preset name (violet, burgundy, pink,
  crimson, maroon, orange, brown, yellow, grass, green, turquoise, aqua, sky, bluegray,
  grey, blue). Panel appearance only.

ops.name: lineStyle
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"lineStyle","color":"#00ff00","thickness":3,"pointSize":6,"style":"dashed"} —
  change the DEFAULT style for new lines (any subset of fields).
ops.also:
- "lineStyle" also carries "pointColor" ("" = follow the stroke), "drawMode"
  ("line"|"rect") and "fillColor" for the defaults of NEW lines.
ops.note: any subset, at least one field
divergence: bot: its bullet advertises only color/thickness/pointSize/style/fillColor, but the parser also accepts pointColor (fixture 029); drawMode is measured only on the editor

bulletVariants.bot:
- {"op":"lineStyle","color":"#00ff00","thickness":3,"pointSize":6,"style":"dashed",
  "fillColor":"transparent"} — change the DEFAULT pen for newly drawn lines (any
  subset of fields), like the /color /thickness /points /style /fill commands.

ops.name: units
ops.bullet: - {"op":"units","value":"cm"|"in"} — display units.

ops.name: view
ops.bullet: - {"op":"view","points":true,"lines":false} — show or hide points and lines.
ops.note: at least one of points / lines

ops.name: clear
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"clear"} — REMOVE the working image and its lines, leaving the editor empty.
  This is what "remove/delete/clear the image" means. Never answer that with
  {"op":"blank"}: a blank REPLACES the picture with a white page, which is not a
  removal. Takes no fields.

bulletVariants.bot:
- {"op":"clear"} — REMOVE the working image and its edits, leaving the chat with no
  working image; the conversation itself is kept. This is what "remove/delete/clear
  the image" means. Never answer that with {"op":"blank"}: a blank REPLACES the
  picture with a white page, which is not a removal. Takes no fields.

ops.name: openUrl
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"openUrl","url":"https://…","incognito":false} — load an image (or video
  frame) from a URL into the editor; "incognito": true loads it into THIS editor
  switched to incognito (nothing is saved), never a second tab or window, so the
  rest of your plan keeps acting on it. ONLY a URL the user themselves wrote in
  this conversation — never introduce, complete, or rewrite one.

url.note: http(s) URL; at run time it must be a URL the user themselves wrote in this conversation

divergence: console and bot bullets do not advertise "incognito", but every surface's parser accepts the field (fixture 034)

bulletVariants.console:
- {"op":"openUrl","url":"https://…"} — load an image (or video frame) from a URL
  as the working image (the console's /upload). ONLY a URL the user themselves
  wrote in this conversation — never introduce, complete, or rewrite one.
bulletVariants.bot:
- {"op":"openUrl","url":"https://…"} — load an image (or video frame) from a URL as
  the working image (the /url command). ONLY a URL the user themselves wrote in this
  conversation — never introduce, complete, or rewrite one.
bulletVariants.extension:
- {"op":"openUrl","url":"https://…","incognito":false} — open an image URL in the Stencil
  editor ("incognito": true opens it as an incognito editor). ONLY a URL the user themselves
  wrote in this conversation — never introduce, complete, or rewrite one; images from the
  page listing open with "open" by index instead.

ops.name: openFile
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"openFile","path":"~/Pictures/portrait.png"} — load a LOCAL file the user named
  into the editor: an image or video, a layout ".json" (drawn onto the current picture), or a
  ".stencil" project. ONLY a path the user themselves wrote in this conversation — never
  invent, complete, guess or list one, and never a directory.

path.note: a local file the user themselves named — an image/video, a layout ".json", or a ".stencil" project; never a directory

divergence: editor membership is desktop-only: the browser does not register openFile — there it falls to the §1 unknown-op skip, so fixture 052 stays verdict-valid
console membership is cli-only: pystencil does not register openFile either
cli and desktop: additionally require an understood file extension (image/video, .json layout, .stencil) and reject a directory — native post-checks

bulletVariants.cli:
- {"op":"openFile","path":"~/Pictures/portrait.png"} — load a LOCAL file the user named
  as the working image: an image or video, a layout ".json" (drawn onto the current
  picture), or a ".stencil" project. ONLY a path the user themselves wrote in this
  conversation — never invent, complete, guess or list one, and never a directory.

ops.name: connect
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"connect","server":"..."} / {"op":"disconnect","server":"..."} — manage the
  user's collaboration-server connections. Only a server the user has already saved
  may be named — never invent or suggest a new address. These editor ops are not
  image edits and cannot appear inside "variants".

server.note: non-empty; resolved against the user's SAVED servers — a plan can never introduce a host

bulletVariants.console:
- {"op":"connect","server":"..."} / {"op":"disconnect","server":"..."} — manage the
  user's collaboration-server connections. Only a server listed in the console
  state below may be named — never invent, complete, or suggest a new address; for
  a server not listed there, tell the user to run '/connect <url>' themselves.
bulletVariants.bot:
- {"op":"connect","server":"..."} / {"op":"disconnect","server":"..."} — manage the
  user's collaboration-server connections. Only a server the user has already saved
  may be named — never invent or suggest a new address.

server.note: non-empty; resolved against the CONNECTED servers

ops.name: reconnect
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"reconnect","server":"..."} — re-establish a connection that went stale
  (the console's /reconnect); the same server rule as connect.

server.note: the same server rule as connect

divergence: cli-only: pystencil does not register reconnect (unknown-op skip there); fixture 055

ops.name: delete
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"delete","path":"old.stencil"} — delete a LOCAL .stencil project file in
  the working directory (the console's /delete). Only .stencil files, never a URL
  or a path outside the working directory.

path.note: a LOCAL .stencil project file in the working directory — never a URL or a path outside it

ops.note: registered by both cli and pystencil; the NAME "delete" is on the bot's forbidden list (server-side destruction) — bot hard-scopes it out

ops.name: copy
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"copy"} — copy the current rendered image to the system clipboard. This IS
  what "copy the result / copy to clipboard" means; never answer that it cannot be
  done. Takes no fields.
ops.also:
- "copy" also accepts {"op":"copy","what":"layout"} — the layout JSON instead of the
  image.
divergence: "what":"layout" is editor-only as measured (fixture 038); the cli console copy takes no fields
console membership is cli-only: pystencil does not register copy (no clipboard wired)

ops.name: removeProject
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"removeProject","name":"portrait 1"} — remove ONE saved local project by its
  name; the app asks the user to confirm before anything is deleted.
ops.also:
- "removeProject" also accepts {"op":"removeProject","current":true} — remove the
  project that is open right now (confirmed in-app).

current.note: must be exactly true — remove the project open right now

ops.note: exactly one of name / current; the app asks the user to confirm

ops.name: clearProjects
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"clearProjects"} — remove EVERY saved local project. This IS what "clear/
  delete my projects" means; the app asks the user to confirm first. Server-stored
  projects are never touched from chat. {"op":"clearProjects","keepCurrent":true} spares
  the project that is open right now — that IS "delete the others / all but this one",
  and you must never clear everything and try to save it back instead.

keepCurrent.note: spare the project open right now — "delete the others"; absent = every saved local project

ops.name: compare
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"compare","mode":"none"|"original"|"vertical"|"horizontal","split":0.5} — the
  comparison view: the original beside/over the edit ("vertical" = side-by-side split).
  View-only; the exported image is unchanged.

ops.name: zoom
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"zoom","percent":150} or {"op":"zoom","fit":true} — zoom the USER'S VIEW (or
  fit to the window). This never changes the picture — cropping is the crop op.

ops.name: renameProject
ops.bullet: - {"op":"renameProject","name":"…"} — rename the active saved project.

bulletVariants.bot:
- {"op":"renameProject","name":"…"} — rename the active server project (or relabel
  a not-yet-saved working image).

ops.name: projectColor
ops.bullet: - {"op":"projectColor","color":"#ec4899"} — the project's name colour ("" = theme).

ops.name: blankColor
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"blankColor","color":"#dbeafe"} — recolour a BLANK project's background,
  KEEPING the drawn lines. "Recolour/change the background" means THIS, never a new
  {"op":"blank"} (that replaces the page and destroys the lines).

ops.name: openProject
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"openProject","name":"…"} — open a saved local project into the editor (the
  app confirms first when unsaved work would be replaced).
ops.also:
- "openProject" also accepts {"op":"openProject","last":true} — the project edited
  most recently, which is what "the last project" / "the one I worked on last" means.
  The app resolves it; you never see the list, so never ask which one that is.

name.note: non-empty; exact match, else unique case-insensitive prefix; exactly one of name / last

last.note: the most recently edited saved project; exactly one of name / last

ops.name: incognito
ops.bullet: - {"op":"incognito","on":true} — edit without saving; only togglable on a blank editor.

ops.name: voiceChat
ops.bullet: - {"op":"voiceChat","on":false} — turn the hands-free voice chat mode off (or on with true); use when the user asks to stop or start voice input / voice mode / listening.
ops.note: browser-only: desktop does not register voiceChat — there it falls to the §1 unknown-op skip

ops.name: chatPanel
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"chatPanel","open":true,"dock":"right"} — show, hide or move THIS assistant
  panel: "dock" is "left"|"right"|"top"|"bottom"|"float" ("float" = a free-standing
  window), and a "dock" on its own opens the panel where it lands. At least one field.

open.note: at least one of open / dock

dock.note: a dock with no open shows the panel where it lands

ops.note: acts on the assistant panel itself, not on the image — the placement its own header buttons drive

ops.name: dialog
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"dialog","name":"projects"} — open one of the editor's own windows for the
  user: "projects" (the saved projects list), "servers" (connections), "shortcuts",
  "visuals" (style & visual settings) or "help". {"op":"dialog","close":true} closes the
  open one. Use it when the user asks to SEE or MANAGE something by hand; when they ask
  for a change you can make yourself, make it instead.

close.note: closes the open dialog; exactly one of name / close

ops.note: the editor's own navigation windows only — never the assistant's provider settings (§13 forbidden); deferred to the plan's end because the dialogs are modal

ops.name: clearChat
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"clearChat"} — clear THIS conversation's history; the app asks the user to
  confirm first, and the clear happens after this plan's other actions finish. This IS
  what "clear the chat / conversation / history" means; never answer that it cannot be
  done. Takes no fields.
ops.note: identical bullet on every surface that registers it; deferred to the plan's end behind the app's own confirm

ops.name: reset
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"reset"} — drop EVERY pending edit and go back to the original image (the
  /reset command). "Start over with this picture" means THIS. Takes no fields.
divergence: cli parses reset (§2 compatibility) but never advertises it — bulletVariants.cli is "" (= no bullet)
browser/desktop do not register reset: in the editor it falls to the §1 unknown-op skip (fixture 054)

bulletVariants.pystencil:
- {"op":"reset"} — drop every edit, back to the image exactly as it was loaded (the
  console's /reset). Takes no fields.

ops.name: describe
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"describe","text":"…"} — set the project's free-text description (up to 500
  characters); "" clears it.

ops.name: export
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"export","what":"layout"|"project"} — send the layout JSON or the portable
  .stencil project file into this chat as a document.

ops.name: focus
ops.bullet: - {"op":"focus","image":3} — scroll image 3 into view on the page and highlight it.

image.note: index into the current scan listing (0-based, bounds-checked)

ops.name: open
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"open","image":3,"mode":"copy","actions":[...],"incognito":false} — open image 3 in
  the Stencil editor. "mode":"resume" focuses the editor tab ALREADY holding that image
  instead of opening a fresh copy — prefer it when the image was opened before (it is the
  non-destructive path); "copy" (the default) always opens fresh. "actions" is an optional
  list of editor operations applied on open, drawn from
  the core op set crop / rotate / filter / layout / page:
  - {"op":"crop","spec":{"x1":"10%","x2":"-10%","y1":"0","y2":"90%"}} — move edges inward;
    tokens are numbers with optional unit % / px / cm / in; a leading "-" measures from the
    opposite side. Include only the edges you want to move.
  - {"op":"rotate","dir":"left"|"right","times":1..3} — quarter turns only.
  - {"op":"filter","mode":"none"|"bw"|"sepia"|"invert"|"contour"|"custom","tint":"#rrggbb"}
    — "custom" is a duotone tint and requires "tint"; "contour" is edge detection.
  - {"op":"layout","lines":[{"points":[{"x":0,"y":0},...],"color":"#FFFF00","thickness":2,
    "pointSize":4,"style":"solid"|"dashed"|"dotted","locked":false,"fillColor":"transparent"}]}
    — draw annotation polylines in image-pixel coordinates.
  - {"op":"page","format":"a4"} — ISO page formats a0–a10, b0–b10, c0–c10.

image.note: index into the current scan listing

actions.note: editor operations applied on open — validated against opsets.extensionOpen

ops.name: attach
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"attach","image":3} or {"op":"attach","images":[0,1,2]} — fetch the image(s) and
  attach them to this conversation so you can look at them (max 8); use this when you must
  see the images to answer (e.g. "which of these is the cat?", "read the chart").

image.note: index into the current scan listing (bounds-checked natively against the listing)

ops.name: pin
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"pin","image":3} or {"op":"pin","images":[0,1,2]} — pin the image(s) in the Stencil
  panel (max 8 per action) so they float to the top of the list; use this when the user asks
  to pin, keep, or shortlist images.

image.note: index into the current scan listing (bounds-checked natively against the listing)

ops.name: unpin
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"unpin","image":3} or {"op":"unpin","images":[0,1,2]} — unpin image(s) pinned in the
  Stencil panel (max 8 per action; local pins only); use this when the user asks to unpin or
  drop images from their shortlist.

image.note: index into the current scan listing (bounds-checked natively against the listing)

ops.note: exactly one of image / images; local pins only

ops.name: scanTab
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"scanTab","tab":2} — scan open browser tab 2 (from the tab list in the context
  below) and REPLACE this conversation's image listing with that tab's images; use this when
  the user asks about a page they have open in another tab. After the switch, indices refer
  to the new listing.

tab.note: index into the shared-tabs listing (bounds-checked; fails when no other tabs are open)

ops.name: rescan
filter
ops.bullet:
- {"op":"filter","search":"cat","regex":false,"kinds":["images","css","video","posters",
  "meta"],"formats":["PNG","JPG"],"minWidth":200,"maxWidth":0,"minHeight":0,"maxHeight":0,
  "markOpened":true,"openedFirst":true,"showPinned":true}
  — set the panel's own filters, i.e. what the list shows. Every field is optional; send
  only the ones you are changing. "kinds" replaces the "elements to include" tick-boxes,
  "formats" the format pills (["*"] selects every format, [] clears them all), and a size
  bound of 0 clears that bound. The booleans drive the three list toggles: "markOpened"
  badges already-opened images, "openedFirst" sorts them first, "showPinned" floats pinned
  images to the top. Use this when the user asks to show, hide, narrow, search
  or filter the listing — never to answer a question about the images yourself.

formats.note: trimmed + uppercased; ["*"] selects every format, [] clears them all

ops.note: at least one field; SAME WIRE NAME as the §2 image filter but a different operation — the panel-list filter (see the core filter entry's divergence)

envelope.note: The plan object (§1). Unknown top-level keys are ignored; "version" is accepted and ignored; a missing/blank reply is substituted. Only the listed shapes are enforced; a variant object tolerates undeclared keys (allowUnknown) — only ops are strict about unknown fields.

extensionOpen.note: The §8 subset allowed inside open.actions: a listed op validates with its override keys, or with the core entry's keys when no override is given; an op named in failOps fails the plan; anything else drops with a warning.
